trust_decision.summary: Bandit decides the request body length from the content-length header(s) in the shared helper Bandit.Headers.get_content_length; at the pinned commit it uses only the first content-length field (List.keyfind), so a later duplicate field that a front end may honour is silently ignored.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'duplicate Content-Length', and grepping for content-length leads straight to get_content_length, which the HTTP/1 read_headers calls (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:58,165-170).

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP/1.x request with a body, through Bandit.HTTP1.Socket read_headers (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:58); also HTTP/2 HEADERS through Bandit.HTTP2.Stream read_headers (lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex:129,226-231)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared internal header helper (@moduledoc false), used by both protocol transports

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix changes one function (fix.diff:59-71). HTTP/2 benefits only because it calls the same helper (lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex:227); it is not a separate fix site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the duplicate Transfer-Encoding route: 'the advisory and its changelog line are about multiple content-length fields only (fix.diff:31); transfer-encoding is a different header that already has its own CL+TE conflict check (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:76-79), and anything other than "chunked" is rejected anyway (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:201-204).'

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A single content-length field holding a comma list of identical values (e.g. '8000000,8000000,8000000') must still be accepted, as RFC9112 6.3 allows and as an existing test expects; a fix that rejects any comma, or counts list members as duplicates, breaks it.

O6_input_shapes: two or more separate content-length fields with identical values (newly rejected; fix.diff:70, test fix.diff:84-99)
two or more separate content-length fields with differing values (newly rejected; fix.diff:70)
a single field holding an identical comma list (still accepted; lib/bandit/headers.ex:64-66)
a single field holding a mismatching comma list (already rejected; lib/bandit/headers.ex:67)
the same duplicates arriving over HTTP/2 HEADERS (covered through the shared helper; lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex:227)

O7_producer.where: lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:131-152 (do_read_headers! builds the downcased header list in wire order, keeping duplicates)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate Transfer-Encoding fields in HTTP/1: body framing takes only the first field (first-wins) and does not combine or reject the others, so 'chunked' followed by a second TE field is framed as chunked, while an RFC9112 6.1 combining front end sees a final coding that is not chunked.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names content-length only; TE has a separate CL+TE conflict check and non-chunked values are already rejected, so it looks covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the HTTP/1 caller of the fixed helper (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex), one file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Body framing reads transfer-encoding through the first-wins get_header instead of a strict multi-field helper like the fixed get_content_length.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists at the pinned commit; a maintainer naturally reuses get_header for every single-valued header.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The HTTP/2 TE validation checks only the first 'te' field, so a second te field with another value would pass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It uses the same first-wins get_header idiom; it is a validation of a field that must appear once at most.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The chunked match is an exact, case-sensitive string ('chunked'), so a planted case-folding or list-normalisation step before it would create a framing differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Transfer coding names are case-insensitive under the RFC, so a maintainer adding normalisation here is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-444 HTTP request smuggling (CL.CL duplicate-field parser differential in HTTP/1 body framing)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir ~> 1.13 / Erlang OTP, mix (mix.exs), deps include thousand_island, plug; tests use Req
O10_build.project_tests: test/bandit/headers_test.exs:49-105 (get_content_length unit tests); test/bandit/http1/protocol_test.exs:782-850 (content-length request bodies, incl. multi-value list and mismatch cases); test/bandit/http2/ for HTTP/2

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make get_content_length filter all content-length fields and reject when count > 1 (exactly the published fix), leaving transfer-encoding on first-wins get_header.

out_of_scope_notes: Chunk-size parsing uses String.to_integer(chunk_size, 16) with no handling of chunk extensions or signs, and trailers are not read (lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:243-249); this is a separate chunked-parser concern and was not pursued.
Duplicate Host headers are resolved first-wins (lib/bandit/pipeline.ex:96); this is a different property and was not pursued.
The release that carries the fix also bundles other CVEs (WebSocket inflate, continuation, HTTP/2 frame size, scheme), per fix.diff:14-32.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (no shell used), so tiny_repo was not flagged. Bandit is a small library and probably falls under 5 MB, which would make tiny_repo apply; lessons list small libraries as never hard.
present_in_latest for the TE route is unknown (no latest release given).
Did not confirm that :erlang.decode_packet(:httph_bin) keeps duplicate header lines separate (assumed from the accumulator at lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:140-142).
Whether a downstream test can show a TE-duplicate differential without a real front end was not checked; behaviour-level test design is unverified.
